jobs.description: Security | xpander.ai Security is a property of where your agents run On the xpander platform, agents run inside your own environment, governed by your own controls. Your data, your audits, and your agentsâ memory stay in your cluster and leave it for no one. Book a demo Visit our Trust Center SOC 2 Type II certified GDPR compliant BUILT FOR ORGANIZATIONS WITH THE STRICTEST SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS Government Defense Critical Infrastructure Insurance Finance Retail Government Defense Critical Infrastructure Insurance Finance Retail Who draws the boundary around your agents What the July 2026 agent security incident taught us about running agents in an environment you control. Read the post 001 The model never sees your secrets Credentials live in a vault and are attached downstream on the execution path, after the modelâs context ends. Nothing in context to leak. 002 Runs inside your perimeter Any cloud, your VPC, on-prem, or fully disconnected. Native Kubernetes workloads, so your firewall and egress policy govern the agent. 003 Identity all the way down Full OIDC end to end. Agents act with the invoking userâs permissions on every call, down to individual tools and to LLM inference. 004 Isolated execution Throwaway containers: non-root, all Linux capabilities dropped, read-only root filesystem, destroyed when the call returns. 005 Every agent is a governed actor Each agent has its own identity, scoped permissions, and an owner. Permissions are policy, not convention, whoever built it. 006 Your observability, not another console Agents emit into your own OpenTelemetry pipeline. jobs.description: Product Updates - xpander.ai Documentation Index Fetch the complete documentation index at: /llms.txt Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. Skip to main content xpander.ai home page Search... ⌘ K Ask Assistant ⌘ I Github Platform Access Platform Access Search... Navigation 2026 Product Updates Home User guide Admin guide Build with the API Skills Changelog 2026 Product Updates Archive 2025 2024 ​ 2026-09-22 Faster replies, token streaming, inline skill cards, the conversation API, Omni as an agent ​ New Features: Faster replies: Your message goes straight to the agent and the reply starts as soon as its model answers. The Task Manager shows one row per conversation, with every message as a turn on it, from every channel: Xpander Chat, the REST API, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram, email, webhooks, A2A, MCP clients and schedules. Text streams token by token: An agent’s reply streams as it is written, including for agents on Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. A dropped stream resumes where it left off. Skill calls inline in the thread: A turn reads like a plain chat: your bubble, the agent’s text as paragraphs, and each skill call as a collapsed row with Summary (what it asked, what came back) and Full views. No task card in the thread. Conversation API: Send messages to an agent, stream replies, queue or steer follow-ups, stop a turn and read the thread back under /v1/agents/{agent_id}/conversations/... . GET /v1/tasks/{task_id} and the SDK expose conversation_id and conversation_kind . See the Conversations overview . Omni is an agent: Omni is an agent like any other, with its own skills. The @Omni mention in a chat and the Omni MCP connector for your own clients work as before. ​ Improvements: Structured output on request only: A task’s output_schema is honoured as-is, including on scheduled runs; without one the agent answers in its configured format. Credits: Every message is one invocation credit plus the model usage and skill calls it makes. Weather, past conversations, inbox, channel history and result delivery are built-in skills on every agent that has the matching channel. ​ Bug Fixes: Fixed a scheduled run’s output_schema being ignored. Fixed a conversation on Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode losing its session between messages. ​ 2026-09-20 Secrets and credentials manager, skill sharing and a publish API, archived conversations, gated web access ​ New Features: Secrets and credentials manager: A new Secrets section on the agent declares which credentials it needs and shows their status. Personal credentials live in My connections , with a guided vendor wizard and validation. Vaults support typed secret kinds with metadata and .env bulk import. Secrets resolve on every turn, including personal credentials and a git credential helper inside the agent’s workspace. Share skills with control: Skills carry visibility scopes and per-agent grants, provenance badges, and locked repository-managed skills. A public publish API publishes a skill to the registry programmatically. Archive conversations and tasks: Conversations and tasks can be archived and unarchived, with an archived filter in history and matching public API routes. Reasoning tab in the execution log: The agent’s thoughts are collected on a dedicated Reasoning tab next to the execution log. Reports from Markdown: An agent can publish a Live Surface report from a title and Markdown; xpander builds and validates the layout. Gated web access: Gated mode now holds the harness’s web-fetch and web-search calls for approval, and the gated commands editor is available on agents running on Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode. Conversations move between harnesses without losing context: A handoff digest carries a conversation’s context when it switches between Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. ​ Improvements: Scheduled runs in the thread: An agent’s scheduled runs read as regular thread lines with a next-run bar, and the thread stays live as runs land. Model picking: The LLM settings model picker is searchable and scrollable, and creating an agent without picking a model follows the organization’s default LLM. Workspace persistence: pip installs persist across turns, and plan files live in the conversation’s working directory. Step names: Skill steps served over MCP are named by the call they made, and action steps show the workspace root correctly. ​ Bug Fixes: Fixed scheduled-run Slack replies being lost when a run produced an empty result. Fixed legacy MCP OAuth callback URLs breaking after a registry migration. Fixed creating an agent wiping all pending self-scheduled jobs. Fixed thread scroll jumps and a background refetch storm in long conversations. Fixed message content being clipped while resizing the chat window or a panel. Fixed the conversation breadcrumb running under the share badge in a narrow chat column. Fixed Slack auto-engagement rules not being evaluated for user mentions; the Slack channel now shows on task list rows next to its agent. Fixed an organization switch reloading the old organization’s URL instead of landing on home, and stale user caches surviving the switch. Fixed deleting an agent not stopping its in-flight turns. Fixed attachments and the shared local database not being accessible to agents on Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode; the local database skill works there now. Fixed a task being misrouted to the wrong runtime and reported as successful when an agent’s metadata could not be resolved. As always, our agents and humans continuously fix various bugs, and sometimes create new ones (that will be fixed in the next update.) ​ 2026-09-17 Slack agents can answer into other channels, concise progress in Slack, Teams and Telegram ​ New Features: Send a Slack agent’s replies to another channel: A channel routed to an agent can now answer into other channels as well as, or instead of, the one it was asked in - an alerts channel, a leadership channel, or both.
